subject: Host deployment suitability & tenant isolation — follow-up
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patel <alex@finnova.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Host deployment suitability & tenant isolation — follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few questions so we can scope the right evaluation:

- Demo takeaways: FinNova liked the latency profile and built-in KV/pass-through caching. Team flagged two gating items for selection between Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC: tenant isolation/data residency requirements, and predictable burst capacity for morning trading spikes.

As next inputs can you confirm the following?
1) Isolation: do you require strict single-tenant hardware (Dedicated or Private) or is logical isolation within Hosted (customer-level tenant isolation + access controls) acceptable for initial pilot? If you need single-tenant, say so and we’ll switch to our Dedicated sizing worksheet.
2) Traffic profile: rough peak RPS and sustained qps, expected concurrency, and typical prompt/response token lengths (avg tokens per request). Example: 120 RPS peak, 30 RPS sustained, ~150 tokens out.
3) Regional/residency constraints: must we keep data in us-east-1 only (or in your EU region)?
4) Rate-limit pattern: do you expect many small requests or fewer large ones? Any hard p99 latency target?

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-page Quickstart matrix (finnova_quickstart_matrix.xlsx) and our Hosted security summary (redwood-hosted-security-sheet.pdf) for your compliance/infosec team.

Proposed next steps: if Hosted looks viable from an isolation perspective we can provision a sandbox workspace with two endpoints (chat+generate) and a 48h burst window for pilot traffic. Can we set a 30-minute follow-up on Tuesday 5/18 to review your answers and outline a sandbox activation plan?

Thanks — I’ll loop Jordan for proposal sizing once I have your traffic numbers.

— Naomi Feldman
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Attachments: finnova_quickstart_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-hosted-security-sheet.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Alex Patel <alex@finnova.com>

Cc: DevOps Team <infra@finnova.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Host deployment suitability & tenant isolation — follow-up

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side (DevOps chimed in on infra):

1) Isolation: For Phase 1 (pilot) we prefer Hosted if logical tenant isolation + strong audit logs/KMS separation is available. If we proceed to production we may require Dedicated depending on SOC/compliance feedback.
2) Traffic: expected peak ~120 RPS during market open (10–15 min bursts), sustained ~25–30 RPS, concurrency ~300 active sessions. Average tokens per request: ~180 (prompt+response).
3) Residency: US-only (us-east preferred).
4) Latency: target p99 < 250ms for generate endpoints; <150ms for embeddings. Burst capacity: need to support 2x peak for at least three short bursts/day.

Follow-up: Please confirm whether Hosted sandbox can be pinned to us-east and whether you support prefix/KV caching on the sandbox endpoints. Also want sample rate-limit and token-based billing estimates so I can flag procurement.

— Alex
Head of Product | FinNova
alex@finnova.com

- Prefix/KV caching enabled for your sandbox endpoints.
